maya: hi folks, day 3 here. building the runtime from source and hit a linker error: `undefined reference to cublasLtMatmul` during `make install`. anyone seen this during onboarding?

sam: welcome! :wave: can you paste the full linker snippet and your `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64 | grep cublas` output?

maya: paste:```/usr/bin/ld: build/liblibruntime.so: undefined reference to `cublasLtMatmul'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status```
`ls` -> `libcublas.so  libcublasLt.so  libcublasLt.so.12  libcublas.so.12`

jordan: that suggests the linker can't find the symbol at link-time despite the file existing. Common causes: building against an older CUDA toolkit headers while runtime uses a newer lib, or missing `-lcublasLt` in the link flags. Which CMake options did you use?

maya: cmake args were: `cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DUSE_CUBLAS=ON` (I didn't set cublaslt explicitly).

sam: try re-configuring with `-DUSE_CUBLASLT=ON` and then `make clean && make -j6`. Also check `ldconfig -p | grep cublasLt` to ensure the dynamic linker sees it.

maya: `ldconfig -p | grep cublasLt` returns nothing. but the files are in `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64`. `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH` shows `/usr/local/cuda-11.4/lib64` from my .bashrc.

jordan: aha, LD_LIBRARY_PATH mismatch. You probably have CUDA 12 libs installed but env points to 11.4. Two fixes: update env to point to `/usr/local/cuda-12.1` (recommended), or add an rpath at link time. For fastest test: `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` then rerun `ldconfig` and try a small link test: `g++ -o test test.o -L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -lcublasLt -lcudart`

maya: did the export, `ldconfig` needs sudo here so I did a quick `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 make` and the link step progressed further but now fails with `symbol lookup error: /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublasLt.so: undefined symbol: cusolverDnCreate`.

sam: that usually means mixed runtimes/driver headers again or a missing dependency (cusolver). Check that `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcusolver.so` exists and that your toolkit install is complete. Also confirm `nvcc -V` and `nvidia-smi` show compatible versions.

maya: `nvcc -V` -> "Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105"; `nvidia-smi` -> "Driver Version: 525.85.12  GPU: RTX A5000"

jordan: drivers look OK. Could be that some system packages installed older libcuda or cuda-toolkit remnants. Quick debug: run `ldd build/liblibruntime.so | grep cublas` to see which library file is actually being linked at runtime.

maya: `ldd` shows `libcublasLt.so => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so (0x00007f...)` which is surprising.

sam: that's the problem: distro-provided libs in `/usr/lib` are older wrappers. You need the runtime to prefer `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64`. Fix by updating your PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH or using `LD_PRELOAD` for a quick test: `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublasLt.so LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH ./your_binary`

maya: preloading made the test binary run further, good sign. for a permanent fix I'll update my dotfiles and request infra to standardize dev VMs to CUDA 12.1.

runtime-oncall: if you want a clean environment faster, we have a dev container image that matches CI: `gcr.io/redwood-inference/dev:cuda-12.1-ubuntu22`. Use `docker run --gpus all -it --rm gcr.io/redwood-inference/dev:cuda-12.1-ubuntu22 bash` and you should avoid host library conflicts.

maya: thanks, I'll try the container to verify. once fixed I'll open a tiny onboarding PR with the steps (export vars, ctest link notes).

infra-bot: ticket created #INFRA-4399 to standardize dev images and add a CUDA 12.1 symlink on dev hosts (requester: maya).

sam: great. also FYI we have a short checklist in `docs/onboarding/dev-environment.md` 90 add a note about checking `ldd` if linker errors crop up.

maya: filing the PR now, and thanks for the quick help everyone! :raised_hands:
